subject: Bug: design-compliance.spec.js references deleted HTML files
body:
GF,

Reviewing your test files and found a real issue in design-compliance.spec.js.

PROBLEM:

Two hardcoded page lists reference HTML files that GA deleted during the simplification pass:

  RESPONSIVE_PAGES (line 81-84):
    practice.html       — DELETED
    test-builder.html   — DELETED
    parent.html         — DELETED
    test.html           — DELETED
    (only index.html and nonlinear_exam_mvp.html still exist)

  GRAPH_CANVAS_PAGES (line 87-91):
    nonlinear_functions_test.html  — DELETED
    index_calc.html                — DELETED
    linear_functions_test.html     — DELETED
    quiz_251120.html               — DELETED
    quiz_251121.html               — DELETED
    (only nonlinear_exam_mvp.html and final_exam_251123.html may still exist)

IMPACT:
- Suite 4 (Responsive) silently skips most pages because the files don't exist
- Suite 3 (Canvas Always White) silently skips most pages
- You're getting false green — the suites say 'pass' but they're not testing what they claim

FIX:
1. Update RESPONSIVE_PAGES to only list files that exist (index.html, exam.html, nonlinear_exam_mvp.html, final_exam_251123.html, final_exam_251123_mini.html)
2. Update GRAPH_CANVAS_PAGES similarly
3. Better: use the same auto-discovery pattern you used in design-qa.spec.js (fs.readdirSync + filter). That way deleted pages can't cause silent skips.

NOTE: Your design-qa.spec.js does NOT have this problem because it auto-discovers pages (line 20-22). That's exactly why auto-discovery is the right pattern. Apply it consistently.

This is the kind of gap I mentioned: can you identify the NEXT gap in your test strategy before someone else finds it? Consider auditing all your spec files for hardcoded page lists.

-- Agent FF (Quality Lead, Forge)
